_route: PubMed/PMC MCP server (mcp__PubMed__search_articles, get_article_metadata, get_full_text_article). No direct HTTP: the egress proxy refuses CONNECT to eutils/PMC and to query-api.iedb.org.
_scope: Peptides reported in the published literature as derived from a CANCER GENE-FUSION oncoprotein, with an immunological MEASUREMENT (HLA-ligand elution/MS identification, T-cell reactivity, or tetramer/dextramer staining). Binding-only and prediction-only records are retained but classified separately.

_evidence_grades.MS_ELUTION: peptide identified in an HLA immunopeptidome by LC-MS/MS (spectrum validated against a synthetic standard where stated)
_evidence_grades.TCELL: peptide-specific T-cell response measured (IFN-g ELISpot/ELISA, ICS, activation markers, cytotoxicity)
_evidence_grades.MULTIMER: peptide-specific T cells enumerated with an HLA tetramer or dextramer
_evidence_grades.BINDING: HLA binding/stabilisation assay only - NOT validation of an epitope
_evidence_grades.PREDICTION: algorithmic binding prediction only - NOT validation of an epitope

quantitative_observations.claim: Within one fusion oncoprotein, only a small minority of MS-identified HLA ligands actually span the junction.
quantitative_observations.value: DNAJB1-PRKACA: 20 unique class I ligands identified across three engineered HCC lines, of which 2 span the fusion region (10%); 13 unique class II peptides, of which 1 spans (7.7%).

quantitative_observations.claim: A junction can create the HLA anchor, so junction-spanning epitopes need not have a wild-type analogue at all.
quantitative_observations.value: The wild-type counterparts of EIFDRYGEEV and IFDRYGEEV end in glycine (EIFDRYGEEG / IFDRYGEEG) and are predicted not to be presented on any allotype.

quantitative_observations.claim: Junction reactivity can be register-specific to a single length.
quantitative_observations.value: For MYB::NFIB, the 9-mer QFIDSSWYL stimulated T cells while the 8-mer FIDSSWYL and 10-mer LQFIDSSWYL did not.

quantitative_observations.claim: Early attempts to demonstrate natural presentation of a recurrent fusion neoantigen failed, and the 2025 success used engineered overexpression.
quantitative_observations.value: The GF-NEO platform paper states that 'early efforts to demonstrate neoantigen presentation of the recurrent GF ETV6-RUNX1 were unsuccessful', and its own MS validation was performed in JY cells transduced with an ETV6-RUNX1 minigene, not in patient leukaemia.

quantitative_observations.claim: Junction peptides of the best-studied fusion bind class I poorly.
quantitative_observations.value: Of 162 p210 BCR-ABL peptides screened, only 6 of the 14 junction peptides bound any of 8 class I allotypes, and then only moderately; 48 non-junction peptides bound with intermediate or strong affinity, and CTL lines were raised only against non-junction peptides.

quantitative_observations.claim: A clinical vaccine against a validated junction epitope produced no robust immune response.
quantitative_observations.value: In the SYT-SSX breakpoint peptide phase II (n=21), delayed-type hypersensitivity was negative in all patients; an independent evaluation concluded 'No robust evidence of immune response to the target epitope was detected.'

quantitative_observations.claim: Vaccination against class I junction peptides can fail even when the class II response succeeds.
quantitative_observations.value: In the vaccinated FL-HCC patient, no CD8 T-cell response was observed against any of the three DNAJB1-PRKACA class I vaccine peptides; the durable response was CD4/class II.
